Article Title: Postgraduate doctors quit premier medical institutes, shows RTI reply
Article Text:
The figures from individual institutions show that departures have continued, even as some reported a decline. (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: Postgraduate doctors are walking away from residency programmes at some of India's leading medical institutions. RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and JIPMER , with AIIMS Delhi alone reporting 34 junior resident departures in 2025.While several institutes lack consolidated data on psychiatric counselling or workplace stress among residents, Dr Lakshya Mittal, chairperson of United Doctors Front (UDF), said multiple RTI applications filed by its members had revealed postgraduate doctors quitting premier medical institutions despite securing top NEET-PG ranks. He cited complaints of duties extending beyond 36 hours, workplace harassment, toxic work culture and inadequate support.“Residency is meant to train doctors, not break them. Discipline is not humiliation and dedication is not exploitation,” Mittal said, urging authorities to enforce working-hour regulations, establish independent grievance-redressal mechanisms and fix institutional accountability. UDF has also filed a PIL in the Supreme Court.However, the figures from individual institutions show that departures have continued, even as some reported a decline.At AIIMS Delhi, 34 junior resident doctors quit in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a decline of about 43%. The number of residents joining also fell, from 324 in 2024 to 267 in 2025. Department-wise figures show the highest number of exits in anaesthesiology at seven, followed by ophthalmology at six. Surgery reported three exits, as did pathology. Ophthalmology had recorded 14 exits in 2024.JIPMER, Puducherry, also reported a decline in resignations. A combined count of departures from its January and July batches shows 44 residents resigned in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a fall of nearly 27%. However, exits continued across several specialities, including anaesthesiology, emergency medicine, orthopaedics, pathology and surgery.The trend is not confined to these two institutions. AIIMS Kalyani reported 15 exits across all three years of postgraduate training in 2025, including 13 from the January and July batches. Another 11 students from the 2026 batches had left by the time of its reply. AIIMS Raipur reported 19 exits from its 2025 batches, AIIMS Patna 12, while AIIMS Gorakhpur also reported departures. At AIIMS Rishikesh, 30 students across various postgraduate and super-speciality programmes left in 2025.The RTI also sought details of psychiatric counselling and whether stress, depression or sleep deprivation were recorded as reasons for leaving. AIIMS Delhi said it had no compiled counselling data, while AIIMS Rishikesh reported six postgraduate students receiving psychiatric counselling in 2026 but maintained no consolidated record of workplace-related stress. AIIMS Raipur reported no residents seeking counselling in 2025 or 2026.AIIMS Patna reported 15 residents receiving counselling in 2025 and none in 2026, while AIIMS Kalyani declined to provide the information, citing RTI provisions.The figures are not directly comparable as institutes provided data for different periods and batches. While they establish that residents are leaving, the reasons remain unclear, with several institutes lacking records that could help explain the departures.
Article Summary: Postgraduate doctors are walking away from residency programmes at some of India's leading medical institutions. At AIIMS Delhi, 34 junior resident doctors quit in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a decline of about 43%. The number of residents joining also fell, from 324 in 2024 to 267 in 2025.

NEW DELHI: Veteran Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and her daughter, Priyanka Gandhi, revisited memories of Diwali celebrations with former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi.In a conversation shared on social media, Sonia Gandhi recalled her fondness for Diwali, describing the elaborate decorations, traditional rituals and festive gatherings that marked the celebrations."Oh, Diwali I loved. So, Diwali was always beautiful," she recalled in a video shared on her Instagram account.Recalling the traditional rituals, Sonia said a Ganesh idol was placed at the entrance of the house, where the first diya of the celebrations was lit. She added that the idol is now kept at her residence."At the entrance, there used to be a Ganesh Murti, which is now in my house. And so, we would do the first lighting of the diya in front of Ganesh Ji's Murti. And it was always decorated. In those days, we didn't have those little lights everywhere, but we had diyas everywhere - around the pond, all along the roof, veranda, and along the path, wherever there was a path. So, it was very pretty," she said.Priyanka Gandhi, the MP from Wayanad, also recalled how festivals were celebrated with great enthusiasm, with people from different walks of life gathering in the Gandhi family's garden.Sonia remembered how the family would sometimes get carried away with firecrackers, while Priyanka recalled how her father, Rajiv Gandhi, would take them to Chandni Chowk in Old Delhi to buy crackers."Papa used to take us to Chandni Chowk to buy crackers. We used to go to Old Delhi to buy crackers," Priyanka recalled.Sonia also remembered phuljhadis, or traditional sparklers, saying she enjoyed them, although she was less enthusiastic about some of the noisier fireworks.Beyond the lights and firecrackers, Sonia said the atmosphere during the festive season remained particularly memorable. Recalling the weather during those celebrations, she spoke about the clear blue skies that formed the backdrop to the festivities."Weather at that time was beautiful. Blue skies and all, which you hardly see now. Yeah, it was lovely," she said.Sonia also recalled that festivals were marked by Kashmiri cuisine and a traditional sweet rice preparation, a culinary tradition that continues in the family."And then, on festivals, we always used to have Kashmiri food and that sweet rice, like that, which we still make, by the way," she said.Sonia Gandhi has also documented several personal experiences and significant moments from her life in her memoir, titled *Belonging: A Journey of Love*. The book is scheduled to be launched on November 10.The memoir chronicles Sonia Gandhi's journey, from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance that brought her to India to the personal losses that profoundly shaped her life and her relationship with her adopted country.In the book, the 79-year-old Congress veteran, who holds the distinction of being the party's longest-serving president, revisits her childhood in Italy, her relationship with Rajiv Gandhi during their time at Cambridge, and the assassinations of her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband, Rajiv Gandhi.
Article Summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and her daughter, Priyanka Gandhi, revisit memories of Diwali celebrations with former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi. In a conversation shared on social media, Sonia Gandhi recalled her fondness for DiWali, describing the elaborate decorations, traditional rituals and festive gatherings.

NEW DELHI: Two days before the India release of her memoir, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi on Sunday described it as “not a political book but a personal one," emphasising that she wanted to portray her family "honestly," as people she knew and loved.“This is not a political book, it’s a personal one. Much has been written about my family, but rarely with real insight into who they were, their motivations, their struggles, their very human flaws. I wanted to portray them honestly, as people I knew and loved,” the Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson wrote on X.She gave a detailed account of how the book, titled "Belonging: A Journey of Love," came to be, in an article for The Hindu, which had published a detailed interview with her on Saturday."For most of my life, I kept my inner world to myself. Even after grief pulled me into politics, I held on to whatever privacy I could, and writing openly about my life felt almost unthinkable. Only after stepping back from the daily churn of public life could I see my own story clearly," Sonia Gandhi wrote in the article, referring to the assassination of her husband, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, who was India's youngest Prime Minister."When I did look back, one thread ran through all of it: love, and the loyalty that grows from it. It all began in England, where a 19-year-old woman from a small Italian town met a young Indian student (Rajiv Gandhi). It carried me into a new country and a new family, into a deep bond with my mother-in-law (Indira Gandhi), and through the years of raising our children," she added,"It also carried me through the unbearable, when I lost first my mother-in-law and then my husband to violence," the former Congress president wrote.Published by HarperCollins India, Sonia Gandhi's memoir will be released in India on November 10, ending uncertainty over the book's domestic publication following an "impasse" between the author's representatives and Penguin Random House India.The book covers major tragedies that impacted the Gandhi family, including the death of Sonia Gandhi's brother-in-law Sanjay Gandhi in a plane crash, Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984 and Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991.The memoir also delves into political events surrounding the Congress' victory in the 2004 elections, when Sonia Gandhi declined to become Prime Minister and instead led the party and its alliance, which governed India till 2014.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi's memoir will be released in India on November 10. The book covers major tragedies that impacted the Gandhi family, including the death of Sonia Gandhi's brother-in-law Sanjay Gandhi in a plane crash. Article Title: Ailing Kerala elephant calf, Maya, airlifted to Anant Ambani's Vantara for intensive hospitalisation
Article Text:
A crucial second opinion brings renewed hope

A collaborative model of compassionate care

Maya, an 18-month-old critically ill orphaned elephant calf, has been airlifted from Kerala’s Abhayaranyam to Anant Ambani's Vantara in Jamnagar for specialised intensive hospitalisation. The calf, who has been unable to stand following a severe fall in July, was shifted to the facility after medical experts sought advanced veterinary intervention as a final effort to prevent euthanasia. This life-saving transfer was initiated when Kerala officials explicitly requested the intervention of Vantara to explore every possible medical avenue.Maya's short life has already been a test of resilience. On April 19, 2025, she was found abandoned as a severely dehydrated newborn near Kaprikkad in the Malayattoor Division. Rescued and brought to Abhayaranyam, she was hand-reared around the clock by the Kerala Forest Department. Sadly, her struggles did not end there. On July 2, 2026, the calf slipped while playing and injured her right shoulder. Despite physiotherapy and dietary supplements, her condition rapidly deteriorated.By late October, she could no longer stand and was accepting only liquid feed. A thorough external examination revealed multiple fractures in her limbs, a chest infection, and generalised bone thinning. Faced with extremely brittle bones and a grave prognosis, a Medical Board made the heavy animal-welfare decision to recommend euthanasia on October 29 to prevent further suffering.Refusing to close the case, Kerala’s Chief Wildlife Warden, Dr. P. Pugazhendi, pursued a wider expert opinion before considering any irreversible actions. After reviewing her X-rays and blood work during a video consultation, Vantara’s veterinary experts identified a potential parathyroid-related disorder that could respond to treatment. With this new possibility, the decision was unanimously made on November 5 to transfer Maya to Vantara. At their facility, she will receive comprehensive pain management, advanced diagnostics, and support from hydraulic lifting systems to position her safely. Stepping in to provide this critical care, Vantara acted on the core principle of Anant Ambani: every life matters, driven by the philosophy of Jeev Seva.What makes this medical mission truly remarkable is the deep partnership built around the calf's emotional well-being. Before the journey, Vantara submitted a comprehensive treatment plan, and arranged an airlift equipped with life-support systems. To ensure Maya feels secure in an unfamiliar environment, the Kerala Forest Department has sent Assistant Forest Veterinary Officer Dr. Binoy C. Babu and her familiar caregiver, Shri Nikhil Babu, to accompany her on the flight.Crucially, her caregiver will remain by her side throughout the entire treatment period in Jamnagar to provide vital continuity. A Kerala Monitoring Committee will closely oversee her medical progress, and once the treatment is complete, Vantara will facilitate her return home to Abhayaranyam.The road ahead is undeniably difficult, and her prognosis remains uncertain. However, with two dedicated institutions working flawlessly together and familiar faces by her side, every conceivable effort is being made to give Maya the best possible chance.
Article Summary: Maya, an 18-month-old critically ill orphaned elephant calf, has been airlifted from Kerala’s Abhayaranyam to Anant Ambani's Vantara in Jamnagar. The calf, who has been unable to stand following a severe fall in July, was shifted to the facility after medical experts sought advanced veterinary intervention to prevent euthanasia.

Article Title: 'First Diwali without Naxal terror': PM Modi celebrates with jawans in Bastar, targets Congress
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated Diwali with security personnel deployed in Chhattisgarh's Bastar region on Sunday. PM Modi credited the forces for their sacrifices in the fight against Left-wing extremism and took a dig at previous Congress governments, accusing them of failing to tackle the insurgency."Because of your sacrifices we have put an end to the terror of Naxalism here," PM Modi said while addressing the personnel.Addressing the gathering, PM Modi said he had come to celebrate the festival with the security personnel as a representative of the country's 140 crore citizens.Drawing a parallel between the responsibilities of soldiers guarding India's borders and security personnel fighting insurgency within the country, PM Modi said internal security was equally important for protecting the nation's unity and integrity."When a nation's internal security is strong, external enemies cannot succeed. However, when internal security is weakened, external enemies also begin to raise their heads," he said.The prime minister then turned his attention to the previous Congress-led governments, alleging that they had treated Naxalism as an incurable problem rather than taking decisive action against it."If you look at the figures from 2004 to 2013, you will find that every year, the number of our brave soldiers martyred was higher than the number of Naxalites killed.Unfortunately, the governments of that time treated Naxalism as an incurable disease and left it unaddressed," he said.Recalling the violence that had gripped Chhattisgarh for years, PM Modi cited the 2010 Dantewada attacks, in which 76 CRPF personnel were killed in an encounter with Naxalites and 44 civilians lost their lives in another incident."This land was soaked in the blood of our brave soldiers. But not a single voice of anguish was heard from those influential leaders living in their palaces. Not a single tear was shed by them," he said.The prime minister also spoke about his tradition of celebrating Diwali with security personnel, saying they were like family to him. He recalled previous celebrations with the forces, from Kargil and Lepcha in the Himalayas to Sir Creek and INS Vikrant.Bastar has remained at the centre of the government's campaign against Left-wing extremism, with the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and Chhattisgarh Police playing a key role in anti-Naxal operations.On March 31, the government announced that the country had been freed from the menace of Naxalism following the elimination of several senior leaders and cadres, alongside the surrender of hundreds of others.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated Diwali with security personnel deployed in Chhattisgarh's Bastar region. PM Modi credited the forces for their sacrifices in the fight against Left-wing extremism. He took a dig at previous Congress governments, accusing them of failing to tackle the insurgency.

Article Title: BJP chief Nitin Nabin asks opposition to follow LK Advani's approach to national security
Article Text:
Nitin Nabin asks opposition to learn from Advani, stand with government on national security

Nabin recalls Advani's partnership with Vajpayee

Ram Rath Yatra and Ayodhya temple recalled

NEW DELHI: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Sunday urged opposition parties to learn from veteran leader and former deputy prime minister L K Advani, saying political parties should stand together with the government whenever the country faces a challenge related to national security.Speaking at a special event at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi to mark Advani's 100th birthday, Nabin recalled the veteran leader's stand in Parliament when the BJP was in the Opposition.“Whenever he spoke in Parliament, he always said that the BJP will be with the government on issues related to the country's security despite being in the Opposition. As a Leader of the Opposition, he said very clearly that the entire Opposition would be with the government when it came to the country. This is something people need to learn even today,” Nabin said.He described Advani as an inspiration for BJP workers and said his commitment to the nation-first ideology had helped shape the party's growth.Nabin said Advani and former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee had different temperaments and personalities, but their ability to work together towards a common goal was unparalleled.He credited the two leaders with laying the foundation for the BJP's expansion from a party with just two Lok Sabha MPs, saying their determination helped the organisation overcome uncertainty in its early years.“As India moves forward into the 21st century, the Bharatiya Janata Party is also moving ahead with its expansion and development. The BJP is working to take forward both the heritage of this country and the legacy of the party,” he said.Nabin also described Advani as an example of the dignity, probity and sensitivity that politics should uphold.“I could not get an opportunity to work with him, but what I have heard from others who worked with him tells me that Advani's life has been an inspiration for everyone in BJP,” he said.He added that Advani had demonstrated immense dedication to the nation despite having experienced the pain of Partition.“He could take even hard decisions with simplicity,” Nabin said.Recalling Advani's role in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, Nabin referred to the veteran leader's Ram Rath Yatra, which was stopped at Samastipur in Bihar.He said the slogan “We will build the temple right there” had been raised by BJP workers and crores of people across the country. Although the yatra was halted in Bihar, kar sevaks carried forward Advani's mission, he said.Nabin credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi with taking that journey forward, pointing to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya as a moment to remember Advani's contribution.“Today, as the country witnesses the magnificent Shri Ram Temple standing in Ayodhya, it is a moment for all of us to honour and remember Shri Advani Ji's historic journey,” he said.Senior Union minister and BJP treasurer Piyush Goyal also recalled his association with Advani, saying the veteran leader never made others feel the weight of his seniority or influence.He said party workers fondly called Advani 'dada' and that the leader had always treated him like a family member, addressing him by his nickname, 'Happy'.“Advani only thought about taking the country and taking the party forward with complete selflessness,” Goyal said, while wishing him a long life.“We all wish that this country continues to get a leader like Lal Krishna Advani,” he added.
Article Summary: BJP president Nitin Nabin urges opposition parties to learn from veteran leader and former deputy prime minister L K Advani. Nabin: Political parties should stand together with government whenever the country faces a challenge related to national security. He described Advani as an inspiration for BJP workers and said his commitment to the nation-first ideology had helped shape the party's growth.

Shri Lal Krishna Advani Ji enters the hundredth year of his life today, 8th November. This year, his birthday fittingly coincides with Diwali , a festival associated with Prabhu Shri Ram and the Diya at a time when we are marking 75 years since the inception of the Jana Sangh, 125th Jayanti of Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee and recently celebrated a hundred years of the RSS There are very few people whose lives have touched so many different chapters of modern India. Advani Ji was born on 8th November 1927, on Dev Deepawali. As a youngster in 1947, he experienced the pain of leaving behind his familiar world in Sindh. He rebuilt his life from scratch without bitterness. This trait of being able to build from scratch, against all odds, has stayed with him throughout. It was seen while he was strengthening the Jana Sangh and later building the BJP. His tenures as BJP President saw the Congress falling sharply from 400 to below 200 in 1989 and the BJP becoming the single largest party for the first time in 1996. Advani Ji nurtured generations of Karyakartas and gave the Party a clear foundation rooted in the principle of Nation First.Two qualities always set Advani Ji apart as a leader. First, his ideological clarity and intellectual sharpness. This was reflected in his speeches and writings.The Jana Sangh and BJP resolutions he authored remain worth reading even today, while his interviews were consistently incisive and precise. Second, the manner in which he exposed the pseudo-secularism propounded by a large section of the Indian polity for many years.Advani Ji took up every responsibility with immense diligence. As an RSS Pracharak, Advani Ji first worked in different parts of Rajasthan. From there, he went to the national capital, where he started working closely with Atal Ji. History shows that it is rare for two towering political leaders to work together for several decades, cooperating with each other without becoming competitors. Advani Ji and Atal Ji set a remarkable example. Together, they changed the course of Indian politics.The Delhi that Advani Ji came to was coming to terms with the horrors of Partition. He immersed himself in making the Jana Sangh stronger. In 1967, Advani Ji became the Chairman of the Delhi Metropolitan Council, where he worked alongside the late Vijay Kumar Malhotra Ji (who became Chief Executive Councillor).In 1970, Advani Ji’s Parliamentary innings began. His interventions have won appreciation across the political spectrum. He made a mark as an MP and later, as Leader of Opposition in both houses and from the treasury benches too. Despite parliamentary commitments, he frequently travelled across India meeting people.I vividly recall the 1991 Lok Sabha elections. It was decided that Advani Ji would contest the Lok Sabha elections from two seats, one of which was Gandhinagar. He had an old link with Gujarat. His father had settled in Kutch after Partition. Advani Ji had also served as a Rajya Sabha MP from Gujarat. So, it was a homecoming of sorts. Being involved in the BJP organisation, I had the honour of helping prepare his papers and assisting him throughout the campaign. The people of Gandhinagar sent him to Parliament time and again. As a voter of Gandhinagar, I also had the honour of voting for Advani Ji on numerous occasions. The care and attention he devoted to his constituency is something to learn from.The Emergency was a watershed moment in Advani Ji’s life. He was at the forefront of saving democracy and protecting the Constitution. His experiences found their way into his book, ‘A Prisoner's Scrap-Book.’ One part of that book, titled ‘A Tale of Two Emergencies’, beautifully explained the striking similarities between the events in India starting June 1975 and those in Nazi Germany in 1933.Advani Ji was a fiery Opposition leader but an equally excellent administrator. When the Janata Government came to office in 1977, Advani Ji became Minister for Information and Broadcasting. It is widely accepted that his work in this department was extremely impactful. As Deputy Prime Minister and one of India’s longest-serving Home Ministers, he was instrumental in strengthening India’s security apparatus. His work in improving the lives of our security forces is remembered with great fondness. His unequivocal stand against terrorism ensured India got a tough anti-terror law.Of course, an iconic moment in Advani Ji’s life was the Somnath to Ayodhya Rath Yatra. It changed the course of Indian society for the better. I consider it a privilege that I got the opportunity to be involved in this Yatra from the ideation stage to execution. Being present at Somnath when the Yatra began was particularly special. A Yatra can be very demanding, requiring long hours, constant travel, physical endurance and an ability to remain focused despite fatigue. Advani Ji embodied this endurance.I also have memories of the saddening moments of Advani Ji’s arrest in Bihar. Then, in Gujarat, the BJP withdrew support from the Chimanbhai Patel Government. With this, a simple message was given, that when it comes to our ideology and the Ram Temple, there will never be any compromise. Many of our senior leaders and Karyakartas took an oath that, come what may, a Ram Temple will be built. And, years later, with the blessings of the people of India, a grand Mandir for Prabhu Shri Ram became a reality in Ayodhya.There is so much more of Advani Ji that is outstanding. His simplicity, for example. After the Navnirman Movement, Advani Ji had come to Junagadh and stayed for a month as an ordinary Karyakarta, preparing the Party for the Assembly elections in which Congress was rejected. He has always shown what probity in public life is about. He is a voracious reader. Those who have spent time with him know how carefully he goes through newspapers. He is a big fan of cinema and theatre, and has been an enthusiastic film critic. His sense of history and the need to preserve it is visible in his book, ‘My Country My Life.’Advani Ji always remained in touch with Sindhi culture. Another effort he undertook was the popularisation of Sindhu Darshan Puja near Leh. I myself had been to one Puja with Advani Ji and George Fernandes Ji.Any account of Advani Ji’s remarkable journey would be incomplete without mentioning Kamla Advani Ji. She was a constant source of strength and support throughout his public life.Growing up in Karachi, Advani Ji could hardly have imagined the path his life would take. In an expression of gratitude, the people of India conferred upon him the Bharat Ratna in 2024. As Advani Ji enters the hundredth year of his life, I pray that he be blessed with good health and that he continues to inspire us all as he has always done.

This year, his birthday fittingly coincides with Diwali, a festival associated with Prabhu Shri Ram and the Diya. His tenures as BJP President saw the Congress falling sharply from 400 to below 200 in 1989.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi appeared to sidestep questions about the Gandhi family's continued control of the party and allegations of nepotism during an interview with British newspaper The Guardian, saying the question of its leadership should be put to the party itself.“You would have to ask the party,” she told the interviewer when asked why the Congress had not moved beyond the Gandhi family's leadership.The newspaper said Sonia Gandhi “skates over the question of nepotism”, quoting her response to the charge that the party is controlled by one family. “We all fight elections: we win them, we lose them. All of us have,” Sonia Gandhi said in a vague answer to nepotism charge.The interview was published on Saturday, alongside an edited extract from her memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", which is due to be released early next week.Sonia maintained that the Congress could still emerge as a credible alternative to the BJP. However, the interviewer noted that many people remained unconvinced after the party's repeated electoral defeats.The article pointed to the Congress's decline under Rahul Gandhi's leadership. After taking over from his mother, Rahul lost the last three general elections to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The party is now in power in only a few states, while the BJP's Hindutva ideology has become the country's dominant political force.The newspaper observed that the Gandhi family's continued control had made it difficult for the Congress to shake off allegations of nepotism and leadership by political elites.Sonia was also defensive when asked about the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government, which remained in power for a decade until 2014, and the controversies surrounding its tenure.“In almost every single instance, the ministers resigned,” she said, responding to the criticism.The conversation also turned to the Emergency imposed by her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi , in 1975.She described the decision as a “mistake” and said she believed Indira herself eventually came to feel the same way.“I know that many would laugh at this, but I believe she was never comfortable in the course of the emergency. I think it was sitting heavy on her,” the ex-Congress president said.Sonia said the Gandhi family was “split on the decision” to impose the Emergency.According to the newspaper's account, her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, opposed the move and advised his mother to wait for the next election. Her younger son, Sanjay Gandhi, reportedly pushed for a tougher response to the Opposition.At a family dinner, Sanjay is said to have warned Indira that the Opposition would destroy her, telling her, “They must be stopped”. His influence over his mother became a major source of public controversy.Sonia recalled that the decision “inflamed tensions” within the family. Rajiv reportedly tried to confront his mother, but she refused to listen.“Keeping Sanjay in check could have prevented much of the damage that followed,” it quoted from her book.Sonia also spoke about the personal trauma of losing her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, who was assassinated in 1991. She struggled to recall how she carried on after his death, with her daughter Priyanka also joining the conversation at her residence.She recalled the assassination of Indira Gandhi in 1984, when she heard what sounded like fireworks before seeing her mother-in-law's body covered in blood and bullet wounds. Indira had been shot by two of her bodyguards.Sonia described trying to revive her as they rushed her to hospital.“There was blood everywhere, and I realised she wasn’t replying to my questions. It seemed as if she had already gone,” she remembered.She described the journey to the hospital as “excruciating”. Despite the relatively light traffic, the drive seemed painfully slow. She said she knew Indira might already be dead because she was no longer responding.Sonia also recalled the trauma and depression that followed, saying she lived “like a ghost”. The conversation touched on Rajiv's private expression of grief during that difficult period.

NEW DELHI: Retired Calcutta high court judge Biswajit Basu has resigned from the West Bengal SIR tribunals, becoming the fourth among the 19 retired judges appointed to head the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) panels in the state to step down.Basu communicated his decision to the chief justice of the Calcutta high court through a letter on Friday, citing personal reasons, PTI reported.His resignation follows those of former Calcutta High Court Chief Justice TS Sivagnanam and retired judges Ranjit Kumar Bag and Indrajit Chatterjee.According to an Election Commission (EC) official, Basu and Chatterjee had been assigned to handle cases from the Murshidabad district.Chatterjee had earlier stepped down, citing the difficulty of travelling around 22 km daily to carry out the assignment. Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: In Noel's crosshairs, Chandra and Mehli reconnect at Tata HQ
Article Text:
File photo: Noel Tata and N Chandrasekaran

Mehli-Chandra meet focused onrebuilding trust, restoring equation

MUMBAI: Fresh from Italy, where Tata Motors announced the acquisition of commercial vehicle maker Iveco, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran invited Mehli Mistry, the late Ratan Tata's confidant and a trustee of the Tata Education and Development Trust, to Bombay House on Thursday.Coming just days after the two were seen together at the wedding celebrations of Mehli's daughter Laila, the meeting reinforced a belief within Tata circles that relations between the two are improving after more than a year marked by a broader power shift within the Tata Group following the death of Ratan Tata.People familiar with the matter said Chandrasekaran and Mehli, who was voted out of the two principal trusts that hold majority in Tata Sons by Noel Tata and others, discussed issues that had affected their ties.Mehli's challenge against his removal is pending before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC).Mehli and Chandrasekaran's conversation last week was focused on rebuilding trust and restoring a working equation. Mehli later left for Dubai, with both sides appearing keen to move beyond a difficult period in one of Tata Group's most significant internal relationships.For much of the past decade, Mehli and Chandrasekaran were regarded as allies.After the dramatic ouster of Cyrus Mistry as chairman of Tata Sons in 2016, Mehli played a key role in the legal fight that followed between Cyrus and Ratan Tata. When Ratan Tata had to choose a successor, he picked Chandrasekaran, assisted by Mehli. Mehli later backed Chandrasekaran's second and third terms as chairman of Tata Sons. The third term, however, became contentious after Noel Tata, who succeeded Ratan Tata as chairman of Tata Trusts, opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment.Mehli and Chandrasekaran's relationship survived differences in personality and style. Those who know Mehli describe him as intensely loyal, fiercely independent and refreshingly blunt. Friends admire his willingness to say in a room what others prefer to whisper outside it. Critics point to a temperament that can run ahead of diplomacy. The redeeming feature, according to people who have worked closely with him, is that his anger rarely lingers.Chandrasekaran is a different kind of leader. Publicly measured and understated, he has cultivated the image of a consensus-builder since arriving at Bombay House. Yet colleagues say beneath that calm exterior lies a highly competitive executive with sharp political instincts and an acute understanding of institutional power.Then came the post-Ratan Tata era. Ratan Tata's death in Oct 2024 altered the balance of influence within Tata Trusts. Disagreements that had previously been settled privately soon surfaced within the trusts.Mehli and fellow Tata Trusts trustees Darius Khambata, Pramit Jhaveri and Jehangir Jehangir argued that information on Tata Sons covered under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association had not been shared with them, limiting their ability to take informed decisions. The four trustees voted Vijay Singh off the Tata Sons board.Concerns about the emerging situation prompted a visit to Delhi by Noel, Tata Trusts vice-chairman Venu Srinivasan, Khambata and Chandrasekaran, who briefed senior government officials on governance issues within the trusts.Mehli, who was inducted into Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) by Ratan Tata and remained one of his most trusted advisers, increasingly found himself at odds with the emerging power structure. He was eventually voted out of the two trusts by Noel, Srinivasan and Singh, who is also a vice-chairman of the trusts.Among the relationships most affected was Mehli's equation with Chandrasekaran. Differences emerged over how developments within the trusts were characterised and communicated to external stakeholders, with Mehli maintaining that his interventions were driven by governance concerns. Communication between the two subsequently became infrequent.People said Chandrasekaran later made efforts, through intermediaries and directly, to reopen channels of communication with Mehli. Mehli remained a respected figure among trustees, a prominent voice within the Parsi community and an influential presence in discussions concerning the Tata legacy.Mehli has challenged the end of his trusteeship before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC), where the matter is pending. He, however, never withdrew his support for Chandrasekaran's stewardship of Tata Sons. In filings before the MCC, he said he had backed Chandrasekaran's reappointment for a third five-year term and was a signatory to the resolution approving it.Chandrasekaran's second term as chairman ends in Feb 2027. His third term is linked to his continuation as a director of Tata Sons, which requires the trusts' approval at the company's annual general meeting (AGM). However, Tata Sons was unable to hold its AGM on Aug 18 after it failed to secure the requisite quorum. The impasse followed restrictions imposed by the MCC on SRTT, preventing it from joining SDTT in nominating a joint representative for quorum purposes.
Article Summary: N Chandrasekaran invited Mehli Mistry to Bombay House on Thursday. Meeting reinforced belief that relations between the two are improving. Mehli was voted out of the two principal trusts that hold majority in Tata Sons by Noel Tata and others. Meeting focused on rebuilding trust and restoring working equation.

Article Title: Jason Kelce's $680,000 home turned into a nearly $6 million Pennsylvania estate, but neighbours are raising serious concerns over his expansion plans
Article Text:
Jason Kelce (Getty Images)

Jason Kelce's $680,000 home became a nearly $6 million property investment

Jason Kelce's 10-acre Pennsylvania estate has bigger family plans

Jason Kelce's mansion expansion sparks neighbour concerns over flooding

Jason Kelce explains why his family needs a privacy fence

Jason Kelce gets zoning approval, but his $5.99 million estate still has work ahead

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jason Kelce's real estate journey in Pennsylvania began with a relatively modest purchase. Today, the retired Philadelphia Eagles star has assembled a sprawling property compound worth nearly $6 million in combined purchase costs. What started as a four-bedroom home gradually became a much bigger family project, with neighbouring properties joining the estate over several years. However, expanding the land brought unexpected challenges. Plans for another house and a privacy fence eventually reached a local zoning board after neighbours raised concerns about construction, changing slopes and possible water runoff.Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce began building their property portfolio in 2018, the same year they got married. Their first purchase was a four-bedroom home in Haverford, an upscale Philadelphia suburb. Jason paid $680,000 for the property, which reportedly had 2.5 bathrooms, a three-car garage, a greenhouse and an outdoor swimming pool with waterfalls and a hot tub.The house also had a finished basement with a fireplace. It later became familiar to fans because Jason used the space to record episodes of his popular New Heights podcast with his brother, Travis Kelce.However, the former Eagles centre had bigger plans for the surrounding land. In 2020, he purchased an adjoining eight-acre property for $3.96 million. Three years later, he added another neighbouring parcel for $1.35 million.The three purchases brought his total reported spending to approximately $5.99 million. Together, the properties created a compound covering roughly 10 acres.It is important to distinguish the combined purchase price from the estate's current market value. The nearly $6 million figure reflects what the Kelces reportedly paid for the properties, not a confirmed appraisal or recent sale.The growing property portfolio is closely connected to the couple's desire to establish a long-term family home in Pennsylvania. Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce have remained in the Philadelphia area even after his retirement from professional football.Haverford also has a personal connection for Kylie, making the location more than a convenient address for the former NFL star. Rather than moving to a different city after his playing career, Jason has continued investing in the community where they started their married life.The family compound also offers room for privacy, recreation and work. The existing home has features that support family life, while the adjoining land gives the couple more freedom to plan a larger residence.By 2025, their plans had moved beyond purchasing additional land. The couple wanted to build another house on the estate, creating more space for their growing family. They also sought permission to change parts of the property and install additional fencing.Jason personally appeared before the Haverford Township Zoning Hearing Board on February 20, 2025, to explain the proposed changes.His appearance was notable because the former football star rarely needed to deal with the kind of local planning issues that come with expanding a large private estate. This time, however, he wanted officials and neighbours to understand why the changes mattered to his family.The proposed construction did not receive an entirely smooth reception. Some neighbours questioned how the work could affect surrounding properties, particularly when it came to rainwater and drainage.One of the main concerns involved removing slopes from the land to prepare a relatively flat area for the planned house. Residents worried that changing the natural flow of water could increase runoff and create flooding problems during construction.Neighbour Wendy De La Rosa raised the issue during the zoning hearing. According to local reporting, she had already noticed changes to her property when it rained.Her concerns were not simply about the appearance of the estate or the construction activity. Water flowing onto neighbouring land could create problems for nearby families, especially if the work changed existing drainage patterns.The discussion became an important part of the hearing.Civil engineer Timothy Davis explained that the slopes were not entirely natural. They had been created decades earlier when a house was built on the land and an elevated section was formed to provide access to a swimming pool.He also addressed the concerns about construction and drainage, explaining that temporary runoff could increase while work continued. However, sediment controls had been put in place, and the team was prepared to direct water towards a more suitable location.The disagreement showed how even a multimillion-dollar property project can affect the wider neighbourhood. For the Kelces, the goal was to create a more private family residence. For nearby residents, protecting their own homes from possible water damage remained equally important.Water management was not the only issue discussed at the hearing. The Kelces also wanted permission to install a fence that would improve security around their property.As Jason's public profile grew through his NFL career, media appearances and the success of New Heights, maintaining privacy became more difficult. His family also attracted attention because of his connection to Travis and the growing popularity of Kylie.Jason explained that the proposed fence was intended to reduce unnecessary foot traffic near their home without making the property look out of place in the neighbourhood.Speaking at the February hearing, he said:"We wanted to be in this area," Kelce said. "We like this area a lot."He also explained the family's security concerns, saying:"Obviously things for my family are quite unique with the security purposes. We’d like to just deter a little bit of the foot traffic coming in and out of the home, so we were trying to put a fence that sufficiently does that while also appeals to the aesthetic of the area and that people would appreciate."The proposal included changes to the existing driveway, a gated entrance and additional fencing. The design team also planned to retain parts of the existing fence and add landscaping to soften the appearance of the new sections.The intention was to balance security with the character of the surrounding street. The Kelces did not want the estate to feel completely disconnected from the community.After hearing from the Kelces, their representatives and nearby residents, the zoning board approved the requested variances. However, the decision came with conditions designed to address the concerns raised during the meeting.The most important requirement involved stormwater management. The Kelces would have to ensure that runoff from their construction work did not adversely affect neighbouring properties. The board also required the approved work to be completed within two years.The decision allowed the family to move forward with their plans, but it also made clear that property expansion comes with responsibilities beyond the boundaries of private land.For Jason, the project represents another chapter in a career that has changed considerably since he retired from the NFL in 2024. His success with the Philadelphia Eagles helped establish him as one of the league's most recognisable centres. His media work and business ventures have since given him a new public platform.His Pennsylvania estate reflects that transition. What began as a $680,000 home has developed into a nearly $6 million property compound through three separate purchases.The expansion has brought new possibilities for the Kelce family, but it has also placed their plans under the scrutiny of the local community. And while the zoning approval cleared an important hurdle, the challenge now is to complete the project while keeping the neighbours' concerns in mind.For a family seeking more privacy, the nearly 10-acre estate may offer plenty of space. Making the ambitious expansion work for everyone around it is another matter.
Article Summary: Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce began building their property portfolio in 2018. Their first purchase was a four-bedroom home in Haverford, Pennsylvania. In 2020, he purchased an adjoining eight-acre property for $3.96 million. Three years later, he added another neighbouring parcel for $1.35 million. Together, the properties created a compound covering roughly 10 acres.

Article Title: Queen Elizabeth II’s final days at Balmoral Castle: Inside the 53,000-acre Scottish estate where she found peace, made cherished family memories and spent her last moments surrounded by nature and lov
Article Text:
Queen Elizabeth II spent her final days at Balmoral Castle in Scotland. (Photo: Facebook)

Why Balmoral Castle was Queen Elizabeth's happiest place

Balmoral Castle has been a royal retreat for over 170 years

The 53,000-acre royal estate was one of the late monarch’s favourite retreats. (Photo: Facebook)

The time Queen Elizabeth met American tourists at Balmoral

Queen Elizabeth continued her royal duties during her stay at Balmoral

Surrounded by Scotland’s scenic landscapes, the castle offered the Queen peace and comfort. (Photo: Facebook)

King Charles reveals why his mother chose Balmoral for her final days

Can the public visit Balmoral Castle?

Balmoral Castle is open to the public during selected months, allowing visitors to explore parts of the royal estate, its gardens and exhibitions. (Photo: Facebook)

Queen Elizabeth II spent the final days of her life at Balmoral Castle in Scotland, a place that held a special place in her heart and was associated with some of her happiest family memories. Located in the Scottish Highlands, the sprawling 53,000-acre royal estate served as a private summer retreat for generations of the British royal family. It was also where the longest-reigning British monarch breathed her last on September 8, 2022, having chosen to spend her final days at a place she deeply loved.Away from the demands of royal engagements and public appearances, Balmoral offered the Queen an opportunity to enjoy a quieter life. Every August, the royal family would retreat to the Scottish estate, spending time away from the public eye. Their days often involved entertaining friends, attending dances, fishing, picnicking in the countryside and going on shooting parties.Queen Elizabeth's affection for Balmoral was no secret. In the 2016 documentary ‘Our Queen at Ninety’, her granddaughter Princess Eugenie spoke about how much the monarch loved spending time at the Scottish estate.“I think Granny is the most happy there. I think she really, really loves the Highlands,” Princess Eugenie said.The late Sir Malcolm Ross, former Comptroller of the Royal Household, also spoke about the peaceful surroundings that made Balmoral so special to the Queen. In an interview with the BBC, he said, “It’s the wide open spaces. No distractions, no aeroplanes, no noise, no traffic. Just this lovely estate where she can freely roam everywhere.”He further explained that the estate allowed the monarch to relax with her dogs and enjoy the simple pleasures of life. “She can relax, with her dogs, just doing what she thought normal people did, and indeed what normal people do,” he said.Balmoral has served as a summer retreat for the British royal family for more than 170 years. The estate was purchased by Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's husband, in 1852. Initially spanning around 17,000 acres, the property has since expanded to more than 53,000 acres.According to the castle and estate's official website, Balmoral encompasses vast stretches of moorland and heath, towering hills and rare, protected woodland habitats. The property also includes the immediate surroundings of the castle, with landscaped lawns, gardens, native plant species, mazes and a nine-hole golf course.For Queen Elizabeth, the estate was much more than a royal residence. She enjoyed spending time outdoors, riding horses and walking her dogs across the expansive grounds. Speaking about the freedom the Scottish Highlands offered, she once said, as quoted on Balmoral's website, “You can go out for miles and never see anybody; there are endless possibilities.”The Queen's relaxed approach to life at Balmoral was also reflected in her interactions with visitors. Former royal protection officer Richard Griffin, popularly known as Dick, once recalled an amusing encounter with two American tourists during a walk around the estate.According to Reuters, one of the tourists recognised that the elderly woman walking alongside Griffin bore a striking resemblance to Queen Elizabeth. The tourist then asked the monarch whether she had ever met the Queen.Griffin recalled that the monarch responded instantly with a sense of humour, saying, “I haven’t, but Dick here meets her regularly.”The tourists subsequently asked for a photograph, and Queen Elizabeth happily obliged by taking a picture of them with Griffin. The incident offered a glimpse into the monarch's playful side and her ability to enjoy ordinary moments away from royal protocol.Although Balmoral allowed Queen Elizabeth to enjoy a more relaxed lifestyle, her time at the estate was not entirely free of official responsibilities. She continued to carry out her royal duties, reading diplomatic papers that were delivered to her daily in the familiar red boxes.The Queen also welcomed foreign dignitaries and British politicians to the Scottish Highlands. The British prime minister traditionally visited her at Balmoral once a year, making the estate an important setting for official meetings despite its reputation as a private family retreat.Queen Elizabeth's emotional connection with Balmoral remained strong until the end of her life. In a speech to the Scottish Parliament in 2024, King Charles spoke about his mother's attachment to the estate and revealed that she had chosen to spend her final days there.“My late mother especially treasured the time spent at Balmoral, and it was there, in the most beloved of places, where she chose to spend her final days,” the King said.However, Princess Anne later revealed that the Queen had once expressed concerns about the possibility of dying at Balmoral, as it could complicate arrangements following her death.In the documentary ‘Charles III: The Coronation Year’, Princess Anne recalled, “I think there was a moment when she felt it would be more difficult if she died at Balmoral. I think we did try to persuade her that that shouldn’t be part of the decision-making process. So I hope she felt that was right in the end, because we did.”Queen Elizabeth eventually breathed her last at Balmoral on September 8, 2022, bringing to a close a remarkable chapter in British royal history at a place that had been particularly close to her heart.Balmoral is now the private property of King Charles, and the royal family continues to spend part of late summer at the Scottish estate. However, the property also welcomes members of the public during designated periods of the year.Visitors can explore parts of the grounds, stroll through the gardens, view exhibitions and enjoy the surrounding countryside. The estate also offers holiday cottages for those looking to experience a stay in the Scottish Highlands.For Queen Elizabeth, Balmoral was never just another royal residence. It was a place where she could step away from the responsibilities of the Crown, spend time with her family, enjoy nature and experience the simple pleasures of life. It was fitting that the monarch chose to spend her final days at the Scottish retreat that had brought her so much happiness throughout her life. Today, the estate remains a lasting reminder of her personal connection with Scotland and the quieter life she cherished away from public duties.
Article Summary: Queen Elizabeth II spent the final days of her life at Balmoral Castle in Scotland. The 53,000-acre royal estate was one of the late monarch's favourite retreats. Balmoral has served as a summer retreat for the British royal family for more than 170 years.

Article Title: A Texas family's decision to donate its historic bat cave ensures four million female Mexican free-tailed bats retain a protected place to give birth and raise their pups
Article Text:
Image AI generated

Why does a Texas cave shelter four million Mexican free-tailed bats

How did the Eckert family protect the Texas bat cave

How do Mexican free-tailed bats benefit the ecosystem

How does TNC protect the Mexican free-tailed bat colony

In 1990, Richard Phillip Eckert and Virginia Eckert Garrett donated a cave in Mason County, Texas, to The Nature Conservancy in honour of their father and grandfather. The gift ensured the bats would be permanently protected. According to the Conservancy, about four million female Mexican free-tailed bats now use the Eckert James River Bat Cave Preserve each year from May to September, and many give birth to a single pup in June. The family set one condition: the land around the cave must stay open to the public for enjoyment and education, as it had been for more than 100 years.According to TNC's preserve page, the cave is "one of the largest bat nurseries in the nation". The page says about four million female bats inhabit the preserve from May through September. Many of the females give birth to a single pup in June. The pups join their mothers in flight at about five weeks of age and stay with them until the colony returns to Mexico in October.The preserve's brochure gives the same figures and names the species as the Mexican free-tailed bat. It describes the site as lying in the Texas Hill Country, southwest of the town of Mason.The brochure says the bats use the cave to give birth and raise their pups before returning to Mexico. It also states that the preserve is home to one of the largest aggregations of warm-blooded animals in the world.TNC's page says the cave's history is closely tied to the Eckert family. W. Phillip Eckert bought the ranch on which the cave stands in 1907. In the early 1900s, he mined the bat guano in the cave and sold it to local farmers as crop fertiliser. His son, Lee Eckert, continued the guano mining and his father's legacy of bat conservation. When Lee died in 1967, he left the site to his wife and children.In 1990, Richard Phillip Eckert and Virginia Eckert Garrett donated the cave to TNC. The preserve page says the gift honoured their father and grandfather, and that it ensured the bats would be permanently protected. The donation came with one condition: the land around the cave must remain open to the public for enjoyment and education, as it had been for more than 100 years. TNC says it is happy to continue that tradition. The brochure gives the same account of the family's history and the donation.TNC's page explains that, like all bat species, the Mexican free-tailed bats play a part in the region's ecology. Each night they search thousands of acres of countryside for food. Each bat eats close to its body weight in mosquitoes and other insects, including crop pests such as cutworm and corn borer moths. The brochure adds that some bat species act as agents of seed dispersal and cross-pollination.These benefits depend on roosting sites such as the Bat Cave remaining undisturbed. Disturbance usually leads either to a roost being abandoned completely or to the decimation of the bat population. Because free-tailed bats have a low birth rate, TNC states that a single act of vandalism can destroy a colony. The brochure says the population has declined dramatically in some areas of the country, largely because of the disturbance and destruction of roost sites by humans. It adds that the bats give birth to only a single pup each year, so the population recovers slowly.According to TNC, it developed a cooperative management plan with Bat Conservation International. The plan prevents people from entering the cave during maternal activity, controls visitation, monitors the bat population and protects the cave's opening. Scientific research continues at the site, and the cave remains open to scientists for most of the year. The brochure says the preserve is an important research site that helps to inform bat conservation strategies across Texas.Each summer the preserve also serves as an educational site. TNC says visitors can watch the bats flutter and chirp around the cave mouth an hour or two before sunset. The bats first fly in a large, low circle and then spiral upwards into a funnel that reaches several hundred feet into the sky. This lasts about an hour. The brochure describes the preserve as "a true wilderness area" with no electricity, restrooms, water or food, and it does not allow pets. It says the cave is about 500 yards from the parking area along a trail that is not wheelchair accessible. The brochure lists a fee of $5 per adult, with children aged five and under admitted free. TNC's page states that the 2026 viewing season has ended and the preserve is closed until summer 2027.
Article Summary: In 1990, Richard Phillip Eckert and Virginia Eckert Garrett donated a cave in Mason County, Texas, to The Nature Conservancy. The gift ensured the bats would be permanently protected. According to the Conservancy, about four million female Mexican free-tailed bats now use the Eckert James River Bat Cave Preserve each year.

Article Title: Why Bengalis in Pune have been flying in delicately packed Kolkata biryani periodically, especially during festive season, for an authentic taste of home
Article Text:
Volunteers from the Bengalis in Pune Facebook group bring iconic Kolkata biryanis to the city for fellow food lovers

Pune:





Kolkata biryani is often identified by its distinctive addition of a large, tender potato, sometimes accompanied by a boiled egg, alongside fragrant rice and meat. But for natives of Kolkata, there is no single version that defines the city’s biryani.Iconic establishments such as Arsalan, Mezban and Dada Boudi have their own distinctive flavours, shaped by their spice blends, cooking methods and the balance of meat, rice and seasoning. A stronger note of clove here, an extra dash of cinnamon in the garam masala, and the taste changes. Each establishment has a loyal following that swears by its own favourite, making biryani as much a matter of restaurant allegiance as regional identity.For Bengalis in Pune, therefore, finding Kolkata-style biryani is not enough. The craving is often for a specific restaurant’s preparation, one that another kitchen cannot quite replicate.For Saumik Bose and Samit Roy, both settled in Pune, the solution was to bring the biryani here rather than keep wishing for a taste of home. In April, requests from friends and members of the Bengalis in Pune Facebook group prompted them to organise a delivery from Kolkata.What began as a community initiative has since delivered more than 1,500 biryani boxes to Pune.“The taste we want is not something we can get at any of the restaurants here, unfortunately. So, we decided to take the initiative for the community,” Bose said, adding, “The arrangement is straightforward. One can place advance orders and pay only actual costs of packaging and transportation, with no profit margin added.”The first step was to approach Arsalan and establish whether the restaurant could prepare and pack the biryani for air transport. After gauging interest within the community in April, the organisers arranged a pilot delivery of 300 packets with a vendor. The response encouraged them to expand the operation.They subsequently approached IndiGo-authorised cargo vendors to negotiate rates and eventually began coordinating directly with the airline’s cargo operation. The restaurant prepares and packs the food before handing the consignment to the authorised cargo team at Kolkata airport. The organisers book the shipment and pay the applicable charges, with a late-night flight bringing the consignment to Pune early the next morning.“Perishable food requires particular care during transit. We tell the restaurants to give it in flight-packing, for which they use airtight containers. We also ask them to remove the potatoes from the biryani and pack them separately. This helps prevent excess moisture from affecting the rice and meat during the journey. The packed food is placed in dedicated thermocol boxes, which are sealed to retain freshness,” said Roy.Weekend deliveries make the logistics easier. Orders are collected in advance and finalised by Saturday, allowing volunteers to coordinate the Sunday distribution. “Some volunteers, including those based in Dhanori, collect the consignment from Pune airport before dividing it by area. Our network then delivers the boxes to customers across locations including Hadapsar and Dhanori. From the initial 300 packets, the operation has grown to around 800 packets per drive. On Aug 22, the team organised a Dada Boudi biryani delivery, followed by another drive around Mahalaya (Oct 10),” said Bose.The initiative has since expanded to Bengali sweets from Girish Chandra Dey and Nakur Chandra Nandy, popularly known as Girish-Nakur. Founded in 1844, the Kolkata establishment is renowned for its jolbhora sandesh, filled with liquid date-palm jaggery. “We brought more than 200kg of sweets, including jolbhora, aam sandesh, mousumi and chandrapuli, to Pune for Mahalaya,” said Roy.The volunteers coordinate directly with the establishments to maintain quality, with restaurant representatives overseeing consignments before dispatch. “An anticipated delivery of hilsa, however, could not be finalised because the fish was unavailable in the Kolkata markets. Our aim is to make specific Kolkata favourites accessible to Bengalis in Pune without adding a commercial margin or compromising on quality,” said Arun Chakraborty, admin of the Bengalis in Pune Facebook group.
Article Summary: Volunteers from the Bengalis in Pune Facebook group bring iconic Kolkata biryanis to the city for fellow food lovers. What began as a community initiative has since delivered more than 1,500 biryani boxes to Pune.

Article Title: ‘Sacrifice runs for Virat Kohli’: Sunil Gavaskar's big take on pressure facing Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer
Article Text:
India's Virat Kohli

Mid-day

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Was Kohli's performance in the first ODI against New Zealand commendable? Yes, he played brilliantly. He could have done better. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Legendary India batter Sunil Gavaskar has weighed in on the debate surrounding Virat Kohli 's pursuit of 100 international centuries, suggesting that a teammate making a personal sacrifice to help the star reach the landmark would bring joy to Indian cricket fans as well.Kohli was in superb touch during the first ODI against New Zealand, smashing 74 off just 51 deliveries to guide India towards victory in a low-scoring contest. However, Gavaskar raised an interesting possibility in his latest column for: had Kohli stayed at the crease for longer, captain Shubman Gill and vice-captain Shreyas Iyer could have found themselves in a difficult position.With India closing in on the target, the two batters might have had to choose between finishing the match quickly and giving Kohli an opportunity to reach his century. The prospect becomes even more significant given that Kohli is chasing the historic mark of 100 international hundreds.Gavaskar acknowledged that winning a match must remain the team's primary objective, but argued that helping a player achieve such a landmark, provided it does not compromise the result, could be a moment of collective celebration."Indians have always been fond of records and so there's always a debate about the rights and wrongs of going for it.One thing for sure that 99% of those who say they don't play for records are actually incapable talent and temperament wise of setting any and so it's easy for them to say so," Gavaskar wrote."There is not a single Indian cricket fan who does not want Kohli to get to 100 international centuries. We are all cheering for him to get there and so, if there's an occasion where some other teammate sacrifices his runs to allow him the chance to get there, the glory will not be just Kohli's but for all Indian cricket fans too," he added.Kohli eventually fell for 74 with India at 124/3 in the rain-affected contest, leaving the team with relatively little work to do in the chase. His dismissal also meant Gill and Iyer did not have to confront the possibility of managing the chase around his personal milestone.Gavaskar felt the two players were spared a potentially awkward situation, including the prospect of facing criticism from fans on social media if India had delayed sealing the victory to give Kohli a chance to complete his hundred."Kohli got out in the 70s. Gill and Iyer were thus spared any blowback if the winning runs had been hit with Kohli unbeaten in the 90s. Yes, it's a team game, but it's also good for the team if one of its members, especially a star player, gets to a personal milestone without affecting the team's chances of winning," Gavaskar pointed out.Kohli, who now plays only ODIs, has 86 international centuries to his name. He is chasing a landmark that remains exclusive to Sachin Tendulkar, the only batter to have scored 100 international hundreds.
Article Summary: Virat Kohli is chasing the historic mark of 100 international hundreds. Sunil Gavaskar says a teammate making a personal sacrifice to help the star reach the landmark would bring joy to Indian cricket fans as well. Kohli was in superb touch during the first ODI against New Zealand, smashing 74.

Article Title: 'Always found her way to the finish line': Family releases obituary for NYC Marathon runner Rachel Apa who died from rhabdomyolysis
Article Text:
Family releases heartbreaking obituary for Rachel Apa who died during marathon in NYC.

The family of Rachel Apa, the 24-year-old runner who died after collapsing just two miles short of the finish line at the New York City Marathon, has released a moving obituary remembering her as a determined athlete who "always found her way to the finish line".Apa, from Lewisberry, Pennsylvania, collapsed near Mile 24 of the marathon in Central Park on November 1. She was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital but died hours later. Her family said she suffered from rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition involving the breakdown of muscle tissue."With determination, discipline, and a heart fully committed to whatever she pursued, she always found her way to the finish line," her family wrote in the obituary.Recalling her final moments during the race, the family wrote that Apa had completed 24 miles at an incredible pace, with a wide grin on her face."On Sunday, November 1, 2026, after running 24 miles at an incredible pace and with a grin that stretched ear to ear, the only thing strong enough to physically stop her body met Rachel on 85th Street," the obituary said."Her spirit was so powerful and full of vitality that not even her body could contain it," the family added.The obituary described Apa as strong-willed and someone who naturally took charge. Despite being just 24, she had already achieved several milestones and inspired pride among those who knew her."At just 24, Rachel had already accomplished so much and given those who knew her countless reasons to be proud. She moved through the world with purpose, always setting high expectations for herself," her family wrote.Beyond athletics, Apa was passionate about animals, particularly her dogs, whom her family described as her "forever children". She was also a talented baker who had created a cookie recipe so irresistible that her family joked they had to get rid of it for the sake of their health."She created a cookie recipe so perfect it had to be thrown away for the sake of our health," the obituary read.Apa was a former Division I field hockey player at Bucknell University. She graduated from the university in 2024 and had been pursuing a master's degree in business administration at Charleston Southern University while working.She was running her first New York City Marathon to raise money for Parkinson's disease research in honour of her grandfather, who died of the disease in 2022.In a LinkedIn post before the race, Apa had credited her grandfather with teaching her to remain active, push her limits and embrace challenges."My grandfather was one of my role models growing up. He taught me to stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges," she had written.Her father, Steve Apa, had earlier said his daughter was in excellent health and had trained for the marathon. He had been exchanging text messages with her throughout the race, but communication stopped when she reached Mile 24.According to her family, doctors told them that she died from rhabdomyolysis, a potentially life-threatening condition in which damaged muscle tissue releases substances into the bloodstream that can cause kidney damage and other complications.New York Road Runners, which organizes the marathon, said a bystander administered CPR after Apa collapsed. Event medical staff also performed CPR and used a defibrillator before paramedics took her to hospital.The New York City medical examiner's office had said it was investigating her death.
Article Summary: Rachel Apa collapsed near Mile 24 of the marathon in Central Park on November 1. Her family said she suffered from rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition involving the breakdown of muscle tissue. She was running her first New York City Marathon to raise money for Parkinson's disease research in honour of her grandfather.

Article Title: Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar, Auqib Nabi to stay back for India’s Test preparations
Article Text:
Indian players celebrate the wicket of New Zealand's Tom Latham.
